related_questions.question: How long will PPP loans be investigated?

text_blocks.snippet: PPP loan investigations can continue for up to ten years after the loan was issued, due to an extended statute of limitations for fraud related to these loans. The SBA can audit PPP loans for up to six years after forgiveness. Investigations can be triggered by suspicion of fraud or other criminal activity and may be extended if additional information is requested.

list.title: Extended Statute of Limitations:
list.snippet: The PPP and Bank Fraud Enforcement Harmonization Act of 2022 extended the statute of limitations for PPP loan fraud to ten years, according to Polsinelli. This means that law enforcement agencies have a longer period to investigate and prosecute potential fraud cases.

list.title: SBA Audits:
list.snippet: The SBA can audit PPP loans for up to six years after forgiveness, and may begin the audit process within one year of forgiveness, says TGG Accounting.

list.title: Factors Affecting Investigation Duration:
list.snippet: The duration of an investigation can vary depending on factors such as the loan amount, the borrower's industry, and whether there are suspicions of fraud or other criminal activity, according to TGG Accounting.

list.title: Ongoing Investigations:
list.snippet: Federal law enforcement agencies are actively pursuing PPP loan fraud cases, says Benesch, Friedlander, Coplan & Aronoff LLP.

list.title: Importance of Documentation:
list.snippet: Maintaining detailed records of PPP loan applications, use of funds, and forgiveness applications is crucial for borrowers, as incomplete or inaccurate records can lead to further scrutiny and investigations, according to PilieroMazza PLLC.
